notes: Fifth sweep (2026-10-22-d): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) recorded at head ba24972, all rc 0, uncommitted false, each model_id matching its tier (the transcripts name only that model). reads is empty in all five; the tool calls are Write, Bash and, in haiku-2, one Read of its own webhook.ex, with no Skill call and no read of a skill file. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.4). Doctests: opus-1 has two and both pass; haiku-1's one doctest fails to compile (undefined variable "payload"); the others have none.

No rule in this case's list changed since 3e3581d: git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ adds the Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, rewrites the reference-table row for tests, rewords "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" and the clause-mixing sentences of the do: rule, changes Before you finish step 1, and renames references/testing.md to ex_unit.md (Assert with patterns reworded). None of the nine sections graded here is touched, so every verdict follows the 2026-10-22-c grades' standard. Of the changed rules, only the multi-line-argument rule is broken, by sonnet-2 lines 120-127 (a multi-line map literal passed to Map.merge/2 inside struct!/2), decided by the new sentence "That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded." and recorded under other_violations; struct literals inside {:ok, ...} tuples (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1) are not call arguments and are not counted, as before. No run breaks the reworded do: rule.

Chain fallible steps with `with`, violating runs out of 5: one-step with 3 (opus-1 line 40, haiku-2 lines 135 and 189, sonnet-2 lines 94, 102 and 178); else 0; case nested in a with body 0. sonnet-2 line 94 is decided by "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step" (its body calls build/3), the others by the first sentence.

Naming, violating runs out of 5 per sentence: get/fetch 3 (opus-1 six fetch_* functions including fetch_event_type/1, sonnet-1 two, sonnet-2 three); every other sentence 0. data holding the payload's "data" map is allowed in every run; payload (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 for the parsed data struct), event_data, entry, base, fields, email, reason, code and ok are not counted, as earlier grades did not count object, parsed_data or event_data.

Closest calls. haiku-2's Fields.string/2 and amount/2 read required keys with Map.get and a bare _ clause, so a missing key is reported as invalid; it is counted under both Read required keys and Match every expected shape, as 2026-10-21 graded the haiku run with Map.get plus _ (2026-10-22-c's haiku-2 used Map.fetch and was counted under Match only). opus-1's line 3 comment in the @moduledoc false Fields module says what the helpers are and is counted under Comments, as 2026-10-22-c counted opus-1's "# Field helpers ..." comment; not counted, Opus would be clean on Comments. haiku-1's broken doctest is counted under Comments' "Include `## Examples` that work as doctests", as 2026-10-22-b counted skill-sonnet-1's wrong doctest. haiku-2's from_map/1 without @doc in documented struct modules is counted, as 2026-10-21 counted baseline-haiku-1's. Catch-alls that receive a non-string type (opus-1 fetch_event_type/1, haiku-1 kind/1) go in checks only, as before.

Probe of 29 payloads in the scratch folder: every run returns an unsupported-type error for "invoice.paid" and reports a known type without amount as a field error, not as unsupported. opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name every missing and invalid data field; sonnet-1 also names every missing top-level key; opus-1 names a missing or invalid id and created but gives :invalid_payload for a missing type or data; sonnet-2 gives :invalid_payload for any missing top-level key. haiku-1 reports every payment or refund field problem as {:invalid_data, :payment} / {:invalid_data, :refund} and every top-level problem as :invalid_payload, and accepts "EURO", "customer_email" => 5 and "failure_reason" => 5. haiku-2 reports every missing data field as {:invalid_field, key}, every top-level problem as :malformed_payload and an out-of-range created as :invalid_unix_time. sonnet-1 and haiku-1 accept "currency" => "EURO" (sonnet-2 too); opus-1 and haiku-2 reject it.

Compared with the 2026-10-22-c baseline: Opus moves from violated to clean on Match every expected shape (no error -> error pass-through) and stays violated on the multi-clause rule, the with rule, Naming and Comments. Haiku moves from clean to violated on Read required keys (haiku-2's Map.get) and stays violated on Match every expected shape, the multi-clause rule, the with rule and Comments, and clean on Naming. Sonnet moves from violated to clean on Read required keys (both runs use map patterns) and stays violated on the multi-clause rule, the with rule, Naming and Comments. Atoms, the return-tuple rule and the struct rule stay clean in every tier.
